content: 1. The title of the classification page should be formatted as (Disease name) classification, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. 2. The purpose of the classification page is to provide detailed information on any condition-specific classification schema that may exist. 3. If the classification schema is minimal, it can be included within the pathophysiology microchapter instead of having its own dedicated page. 4. For an example of a microchapter on classification, refer to the provided link. 5. At the top of the edit box for all microchapter pages linked to the main page, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template you created. 6. Ensure that links within WikiDoc are created by placing brackets around key terms you want to link to other pages. Make these links as specific as possible. For instance, if a sentence mentions anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than just anterior, artery, or syndrome. 7. For more information on creating links, refer to the provided link. 8. Classification is distinct from the natural history of a disease. For example, primary, secondary, and tertiary syphilis fall under the natural history of disease as they represent the chronological progression of the same illness. In contrast, hepatic encephalopathy and hypoxic encephalopathy fall under the classification of encephalopathy. 9. Follow the same formatting and capitalization guidelines as outlined in the provided template. 10. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. Overview Section 11. The overview section must include the disease name in the first sentence. 12. The goal of the overview is to summarize the page in a few sentences, typically outlining the categories by which the disease is classified. 13. For an example of an overview, refer to the provided link. Classification Section 14. In the classification section, list the categories under which the disease can be classified and provide a brief description of each. 15. Diseases may be classified at a pathological level based on their manifestations or appearance. 16. For an example of a page with multiple classification schemes, refer to the provided link. Staging of Malignant Diseases 17. For malignant diseases classified using staging systems, use the provided template when adding content to the classification page. 18. Include a table or section that outlines the different stages and provides a definition for each stage. The level of detail may vary depending on the complexity of the staging system. 19. Provide proper in-text and end-of-text citations for all staging systems to avoid plagiarism. 20. If a malignant disease does not have a staging system, explicitly state this in the classification page by writing: There is currently no staging system for [disease name]. 21. Note that staging of a malignant disease is NOT synonymous with grading of the disease. These terms should not be used interchangeably. 22. Staging describes the spread and extent of the disease, usually based on clinical features and imaging findings. For example, the TNM (Tumor-Node-Metastasis) system is a common staging system. 23. The disease stage should be included in the Stage microchapter for that disease. Grading of Malignant Diseases 24. Grading describes the pathological features of cancer cells, such as differentiation or rate of growth, based on histopathological analysis. 25. For example, prostate cancers are graded using the Gleason grading system. Preferred Template Statements 26. If there is no classification system for the disease, state: There is no established system for the classification of [disease name]. 27. If there is a classification system with multiple subgroups, state: [Disease name] may be classified according to [criteria] into subtypes/groups: [list subtypes/groups]. 28. If the disease is classified as acute or chronic, state: Based on the duration of symptoms, [disease name] may be classified as either acute or chronic. 29. If the disease is classified based on malignancy, provide a detailed description of the staging system, including the stages, their definitions, and any associated findings. 30. If the staging system does not conform to the standard template, use a custom statement and elaborate in your own words.
